patient_summary: Synthetic demo patient J. Alvarez, 46, with 3 weeks of mechanical low back pain (M54.5). The pain is dull, rated 4/10, and makes bending and prolonged sitting difficult. Radiation, numbness, weakness, bowel/bladder change, trauma and malignancy history are all documented as absent.
request_summary: Dr. Karen Wu, DPT (Lakeside Physical Therapy Group) requests outpatient PT: 1 evaluation plus 8 therapeutic-exercise visits (97110) at 2x/week for 4 weeks. The patient was referred by PCP Dr. Sandra Lee.
met_criteria: PT-EVAL-001: A qualified provider has referred the patient. The notes document a referral by PCP Dr. Sandra Lee for PT evaluation and treatment.
PT-EVAL-001: A functional limitation is documented. The notes describe difficulty bending and with prolonged sitting, with pain 4/10, related to low back pain.
PT-EVAL-001: No red flags requiring urgent escalation. The review of systems is negative, with no neurological deficit and no trauma or malignancy history.
PT-EVAL-001: No more than 3 initial evaluation visits. Only 1 evaluation is requested.
unmet_criteria: PT-EVAL-001 'standard treatment frequency': unclear rather than unmet. 2x/week for 4 weeks is requested, but the policy gives no numeric definition of standard frequency.
reviewer_focus_areas: Does 2x/week for 4 weeks (8 visits) count as the plan's standard treatment frequency under PT-EVAL-001?
The notes request an initial evaluation, but only 97110 is listed. Should an evaluation code (97161-97163) be added to the request?
Confirm the ordering NPI belongs to the requesting provider.
citations: PT-EVAL-001: A qualified provider has referred the patient for physical therapy evaluation and/or treatment.
PT-EVAL-001: The clinical notes describe a functional limitation (pain, weakness, reduced range of motion, or difficulty with activities of daily living) related to the diagnosis.
PT-EVAL-001: No more than 3 initial evaluation visits and standard treatment frequency are being requested (higher frequency/duration requests route to standard review).
PT-EVAL-001: No red flags requiring urgent escalation (e.g., acute neurological deficit, suspected fracture) are present.
risk_flags: Minor internal inconsistency: an evaluation visit is requested but no evaluation procedure code is listed.
rationale: Three criteria are clearly documented, and the evaluation count is within the limit. The remaining judgment is whether the requested frequency is 'standard', which the policy does not quantify, so a nurse should confirm it. Confidence is a self-reported estimate, not measured accuracy. SYNTHETIC DEMO.
